AGENTS.md: The single source of the rules for every coding agent: workflow, working agreements, conventions, commands. Fill in its "Code conventions" section.
CLAUDE.md: One line, `@AGENTS.md`, that makes Claude Code read the shared rules. Room below it for Claude-only notes.
GEMINI.md: One line, `@./AGENTS.md`, that makes Gemini CLI read the shared rules. Room below it for Gemini-only notes.
.github/copilot-instructions.md: A short, self-contained digest of the rules for Copilot (which does not expand imports). Kept under about 4,000 characters.
Short Copilot rules that apply only to test files (matched by an `applyTo` pattern).
.github/instructions/docs.instructions.m: Short Copilot rules that apply only to documentation files.
@@component_path@@/AGENTS.md: The component's own commands and conventions. Agents working in that folder read it as well as the root file.
@@component_path@@/CLAUDE.md: Imports the component's `AGENTS.md` for Claude Code.
@@component_path@@/GEMINI.md: Imports the component's `AGENTS.md` for Gemini CLI.
Short Copilot rules for the component's folder.
README.md: A skeleton README. If you already have one, yours is kept and this one is not written.
CONTRIBUTING.md: The workflow from need to release as a drawing, a "what do I do" table, what is checked where, and the commit rules.
SECURITY.md: How to report a vulnerability, and a place to say what the software reaches.
SUPPORT.md: Where to ask for help, and what to include in a bug report.
CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md: The Contributor Covenant 2.1, with your contact.
LICENSE: The MIT licence, with the year and your name.
ROADMAP.md: Ideas, not promises: next, later, and set aside with the reason.
.editorconfig: Editor settings (indentation, line endings), with a section where a component's indentation differs.
.gitignore: Your file gains the lines the stack needs (build folders, `.env`); lines of yours are never removed.
@@component_path@@/.nvmrc: Pins the Node version for the component, read by CI and by version managers.
@@component_path@@/rust-toolchain.toml: Pins the Rust channel with rustfmt and clippy, read by CI and by rustup.
@@component_path@@/.python-version: Pins the Python version for the component, read by CI and by version managers.
docs/EVOLVING.md: The path every change follows, from idea to release, step by step.
docs/ENGINEERING.md: A skeleton for how the project is built: overview, layout, rules the code enforces, services.
docs/adr/template.md: The template for a new decision record.
docs/adr/0002-conventional-commits-and-a: Why commits and pull request titles follow Conventional Commits.
docs/adr/0003-one-agent-instruction-file: Why `AGENTS.md` is the single source and the other agent files only point to it.
.github/pull_request_template.md: The pull request description: summary, decision, what was verified, what was not, a checklist.
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml: Turns off blank issues and points vulnerability reports to the private advisory page.
.github/CODEOWNERS: Who reviews what: you for everything, and an owner per component when you named one.
.github/dependabot.yml: Weekly dependency updates, one entry per component folder, with pull request titles that pass the commit rules.
.github/workflows/ci.yml: CI: a job per component that runs only when its folder changed, the commit-message check, and one final job, `Quality gate`, to make required.
.github/workflows/pr-title.yml: Checks that the pull request title follows Conventional Commits (it becomes the squash commit).
.github/workflows/codeql.yml: CodeQL code scanning, one matrix entry per language. Free on public repositories; needs GitHub Code Security on private ones.
.github/workflows/release.yml: release-please: keeps a release pull request up to date with the version and the changelog.
release-please-config.json: release-please settings: one package per component, changelog sections.
.release-please-manifest.json: The current version of each package, which release-please updates.
.githooks/commit-msg: Refuses a commit message that is not a Conventional Commit (and, if you chose, one with an attribution trailer).
.githooks/pre-commit: Refuses a commit on the default branch (the very first commit excepted).
.githooks/pre-push: Refuses a push to the default branch, then runs the quality gate (`quality.sh --changed` in a monorepo).
scripts/conventional-commit-check.sh: The commit-message rule, written once; used by the hook and by CI.
scripts/check-commit-messages.sh: Runs that rule over every commit of a pull request, for CI.
scripts/setup-hooks.sh: Installs the hooks once per clone (`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`).
scripts/quality.sh: Runs the quality gate of each component, whole or for what a branch changed.
scripts: The spec reviewer: dependency-free Node scripts that check specs against code (`scripts/spec-review.ts` and `scripts/spec-review/`).
openspec/README.md: How to write and change a spec, and when a proposal is worth it.
openspec/code-map.json: Ties code and test files to the capabilities they implement.
openspec/spec-template.md: The template for a new capability spec.
.github/workflows/specs.yml: CI for specs: they validate, and a change to code comes with a change to a spec (or the `no-spec` label).
docs/adr/0004-specs-are-checked-in-ci.md: Why specs are checked in CI and how drift is detected.
.env.example: Settings for the optional local model of the spec review. Appended to, never replaced.
flake.nix: A Nix dev shell with the toolchains of every component plus git, gh and jq.
.envrc: `use flake`: direnv loads the dev shell when you enter the folder.
